thread:
tayler-cs: Heads-up — AcmePay reported that after last night's rollout their integration started returning responses that omit function calls entirely or pass wrong args. They reported 5 failures in the last 2 hours. Customer is escalated and blocking a release. sample request id: rq_8b1f2c. They say behavior matched our previous model last week.

julie-support: Ack. Can you paste the example payload and the response they got? Also what model alias were they on?

tayler-cs: Pasting redacted snippet from the customer (they masked PII):

```json
// request (customer)
{
  "model": "redwood-chat-v2.3.0",
  "input": "Charge customer for order 12345. If card fails, call refund_processor(amount, reason).",
  "tools": ["refund_processor"],
  "functions": [
    {"name":"refund_processor","params":{"amount":"number","reason":"string"}}
  ]
}

// response (customer saw)
{
  "id":"resp_...",
  "output":"Card failed, logged error.",
  "tool_call": null
}
```

They say previously model returned an explicit tool call: `tool_call: {name: \"refund_processor\", args: {amount: 100.0, reason: \"card_declined\"}}`.

samir-eng: Thanks. Two quick data points: we rolled a runtime change to batching KV pruning at 2026-03-14T23:40Z (canary id c-20260314-11) which targeted token-level suppression heuristics. That could affect function-call detection if the model pattern matching spans cached prefixes. Can we get the full server-side request id? tayler?

tayler-cs: They provided `rq_8b1f2c` and a second one `rq_8b9d77` where args were malformed (amount came through as string "100" instead of number). Customer claims it started immediately after that deploy.

maria-runtime: I'm pulling logs for those request ids. Quick note: the canary did change the prefix compacting behavior which can shift absolute token indices. Possible the function call signal got truncated or the tokenizer boundaries changed for certain prompts. I'm grabbing model-infer traces now.

deploy-bot: Deployment c-20260314-11 -> rollout started by @samir-eng at 2026-03-14T23:40:12Z; 20% ramp -> 100% complete at 2026-03-15T00:12:03Z.

alex-ml: Running local repro against the exact prompt + functions:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxx' -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-v2.3.0","input":"Charge customer for order 12345. If card fails, call refund_processor(amount, reason).","functions":[{"name":"refund_processor","params":{"amount":"number","reason":"string"}}]}' | jq
```

On my machine I see `tool_call` present when I pin to tag `redwood-chat-v2.3.0@stable-20260301`, but when I hit the `latest` alias (which points to the post-canary runtime) I sometimes get `tool_call: null` or the args as strings. Repro is intermittent but consistent across ~40% of runs.

samir-eng: That matches Maria's suspicion. Two hypotheses: 1) Token boundary changes cause function-call parser to miss the span that indicates an explicit call; 2) The post-canary runtime applies a normalization step that coerces numeric tokens to strings in some quantized execution path.

ryan-sre: I'm seeing the same in infra logs: for rq_8b1f2c we have an intermediate postprocess stage `parse_function_call` returning empty result for one replica family (rA3) but success on rB2. Replica mapping: rA3 used the new kernel set `k-quant-1b`, rB2 used `k-legacy-0`.

ops: Proposing immediate mitigation: route AcmePay to `redwood-chat-v2.3.0@stable-20260301` (pre-rollout variant) and open an incident P1 to investigate the kernel/runtime delta. Can we do a targeted route?

maria-runtime: Yes we can add routing rule for account `acmepay` to pin to `stable-20260301` via feature-flag routing. I'll prepare the rule and deploy in 10m. Also will add additional logging on `parse_function_call` to capture token spans.

julie-support: I'll send the customer a patch note: short-term we're pinning them to stable variant. Ask them to provide any more request ids and to set header `X-Debug: true` to get expanded traces if they can. Draft: "We've pinned your traffic to a stable model variant and are investigating a regression introduced in the last rollout. Could you enable debug headers for 1-2 failing requests and share the ids?"

samir-eng: For longer-term fix we should: (A) audit tokenization changes between kernels, (B) add unit tests that include function-calling signal patterns across tokenization/quantization variants, (C) consider conservative fallback: if parse fails but model output contains function-like JSON, attempt a secondary serializer that tolerates stringified numbers.

alex-ml: I'll add a quick test harness that fuzzes around token boundaries and runs against both kernel families. If we can reproduce locally 100% we can push a hotfix to the runtime.

ryan-sre: Opening incident INC-2026-0315-01, escalated to oncall. Routing rule queued.

deploy-bot: Feature flag update for routing rule queued by @maria-runtime at 2026-03-15T00:45:10Z.

maria-runtime: Routing rule applied for account acmepay -> `stable-20260301`. Confirmed via routing logs: 100% traffic now pinned.

julie-support: Customer notified and confirmed they see the old behavior restored for new requests. They're going to replay two failing requests with `X-Debug: true` and share ids.

tayler-cs: Thanks team — please post updates here once you have traces from `parse_function_call` and any repro that explains numeric coercion vs token truncation. Customer is holding a release so prefer a short RCA and ETA.

samir-eng: Will follow up with root cause once ML tokenization diff and kernel change reviews complete. Preliminary ETA for root cause analysis: ~8 hours. Hotfix ETA if we can reproduce reliably: ~24-48 hours.

alex-ml: Added a repro run and saw that when tokenizer splits `refund_processor(amount, reason)` across a quant boundary the JSON pointer for args loses number typing. Dumped the tokenizer byte offsets and pushing patch to test harness.

ryan-sre: Incident updated: notes + mitigation steps + owner list. Assigning samir-eng and alex-ml.

julie-support: I'll keep customer updated every 2 hours.

tayler-cs: Appreciate it. :thumbsup:
